finding.text: The task folder has no top-level `requirements.md`; the owner's ask for the Mention change ("anything referenceable is clickable, never only a code snippet") is stated only inside `ext/Mention/doc/Mention-notes.md`. A fresh agent cannot check the diff against the owner's words, so add a `requirements.md` (or `plan.md` section) that quotes it and links the prompt.

The diff touches only `ext/Mention/`, yet the folder holds three briefs (`reader/`, `roles/`, `routing/`). `roles/` has no report, proposal or `log` line in its folder, and `reader/` is only a design in `plan.md` with no link from `reader/requirements.md` to it, so what landed and what is open can't be read from the folder alone. Add a short `report.md` per brief, or an index in `plan.md`.

`ext/Mention/readme.md` (lines 4 and 21) still says only "a person or an agent role"; it never says that `@mastermind-x`/`task-mastermind-*`-shaped live agent ids now link, nor that a code span holding only a reference is upgraded. `doc/Mention-notes.md` was updated, but `doc/syntax.md` (the syntax rules) does not mention the code-span rule or the agent link, so it is now stale on "code is left alone".

`Mention.js:108` and `upgrade_code` accept any bare `assistant…` word: `AGENT_KIND` has `/^assistant/`, so inline code like `assistant` or `assistants` (and `minion-` prefixes in prose code) turns into a link to `/framework/ai/sessions/assistant/` that opens no agent. Only upgrade a bare (no `@`) code span when it matches a stricter id shape (for example `assistant-<name>`), or require the `@`.
`upgrade_code` (`Mention.js:216`) bypasses `skip()`, so a `code` inside a `textarea`, or any editable surface, would be rewritten too; harmless today, but the walk below it honours `SKIP_TAGS`.

`mention_html` (the string form) does not apply the code-span upgrade, so `mentions(el)` and `mention_html` now differ on `` `@owner` ``; say so in `Mention-notes.md` or it will surprise the next reader.

No test or screenshot covers the new behaviour; `shots/` holds only `framework-1920.png` and `framework-ext-Chat-v2-1920.png`, neither of which shows a code-span mention. A one-line check in the demo page would prove it.

Simpler path: the same effect could be had by dropping `CODE` from `SKIP_TAGS` only for whole-text matches, instead of a second pass over every `code` element, but the current pass is small and clear; leave it unless it shows up in profiles.

The task folder has no top-level `requirements.md`; the asks live only in `reader/`, `roles/`, `routing/` and the handoff, so a fresh agent cannot see the numbered asks from `plan.md` alone (it points at "the spawn prompt"). Add one `requirements.md` that lists asks 1-10 in the owner's words, or link them from `plan.md`.

The diff delivers only step 1 of A (the V2 model fixes, the tests, two docs), yet `plan.md` row A reads "review and merge" as if the reader work were finished. The ask was ONE shared reader for V1, V2 and the session page; step 2 was stopped by the size rule and the decision to keep V1 on its own shape is only in `reader/design.md`. Say in `plan.md` that the one-reader ask is deferred to E and that the owner's "one reader" was not met by this diff.

`ext/Chat/v2/readme.md:110` (diff) says 47 checks, but the diff adds three `check()` calls to `ChatV2.test.mjs` on a readme that said 43, which makes 46. Run the test and put in the real number, since the readme is meant to be verified.

`ChatV2.test.mjs` `check("paragraphs.replace…", true)` and `check("raw.push with an array…", true)` are always true after the `waitForFunction`. They fail only by timeout throwing, which is fine, but the failure then reads as a crash and not a failed check.

The new `core/Task/sentences.js` splitter also splits on newlines and on whitespace after `.!?…` where the old regex did not. A fixture reply anchored to an old id such as `a3` could now point at different words. The doc already lists "a rewrite renumbers sentences" (defect 6), but run the 43 existing checks (they were not shown) to confirm no fixture anchor moved.

`prompt-record.md:44-45` (diff context) still calls V1's `Widget.Thread` and defects 1, 2, 6, 7 open; that is accurate. The main-tree copy still shows the old "replace ignored" rows until this merges, so merge before anyone reads it.

The simpler path in `ChatV2Model.js:78-81` is fine: it drops one regex and adds an import. Nothing broken found in the `raw`, `paragraphs.add` and `paragraphs.replace` branches. The two new screenshots under `session-d3ed399d/minion-minion-chat-reader/shots/` were not inspected, and the minion's folder holds only `past-work.md` and `session.jsonl` (no readme or report), so link them from this task's `plan.md`.

finding.text: The hallucination guard checks `this.has_speech` at final-text time (ext/Chat/Mic.js, the `is_hallucination(text) && !this.has_speech` line), but ux/Dictate/Dictate.js:526 (`close_segment`) sets `has_speech = false` synchronously before the async whisper final returns. So the flag is almost always false when a final arrives, and a genuinely spoken "Thank you." or "Bye." is dropped, which breaks the stated "never touches real speech" promise. Capture `has_speech` per segment (e.g. on the pending item at close) and test that.

`cut_re()` (ext/Chat/Mic.js, new method near line 654) drops `!` and `…` from the cut set whenever any of the three new checkboxes is on. A sentence ending in "!" or "…" is no longer cut, while `ends_sentence` (Mic.js:159) still counts it. Also `send_on_comma` defaults to true, so every comma now cuts a send, which fragments sentences into pieces. Include `!` and `…` with the period, and default comma off.

The new settings `send_on_period`, `send_on_question` and `send_on_comma` are not in `ext/Chat/doc/mic-notes.md`, which documents `sentences_per_send` and the other gear settings (around line 294). The doc and the code have drifted, so a fresh agent would not know the new settings exist. The comments say "deliverable 15", but requirements.md has no item 15; the source of the ask is not traceable from the task folder.

Asks 3 (cards converge), 5 (offscreen cue), 7 (fast-seat Question-only, smart-seat titles), 8 (windowed list) and the shared reader (ask 1) are not in this diff. plan.md says A is deferred and B, D and E are in review or waiting. The folder does not say what remains, so a fresh agent cannot continue from it. Add a status line per numbered ask to requirements.md or plan.md.

The `.claude/skills/voice-assistant/SKILL.md` change makes the fast seat set `edit: improve` on every sentence. That contradicts ask 7, "fast seat places per sentence and makes Question items only". It also conflicts with ux/Dictate/doc/wake-policy.md:37 (plan.md notes it is stale). The wake-policy doc and the roles brief need to agree with the skill.
ext/Chat/v2/fixture/dbg-27008.jsonl is an untracked debug file in the module (git status). Remove it or index it in the module's docs.

Ask 2 says a mark appears "only when pending or wrong". Chat.js `sent_badge` now shows a standing green ✓ or ✓✓ on every sent message, in the bubble chat (Chat.css `.chatbox-sent`). In V2 the badge still shows ✓ once a node is sent. This reads as a design choice (messenger ticks, per the owner's later wording), but it differs from the written ask. The comment in Chat.js:56 records the alternative, which is good. The comment claims "nothing shows until the first tick" while the V2 css comment says "waiting …", which is inconsistent: `sent_badge` returns null when nothing is sent, so no "waiting" mark exists in either chat.

`working_dots` (ext/Chat/v2/ChatV2.js:190) is implemented, but nothing in this diff writes `working:{by,at}`, and I found no staleness limit. If the smart seat dies, the pulse stays on forever. Consider honouring `working.at` age.
The Chat.css comment blocks are long (6 lines) against the rule of one short line per comment, and they narrate task history.

ChatV2.js render (diff line ~250): `smart_dots` is created only after the `if (!roots.length) return div.c("chat-v2-empty"...)` early return, so a chat that starts empty never gets the 🧠 indicator when its first Prompt arrives (apply_one then skips it because `this.smart_dots` is undefined). Create it outside the empty branch; ask 6 fails for new sessions.

Ask 2 says a per-message mark only when pending or wrong, but the bubble chat's `sent_badge` (Chat.js) now leaves a standing "✓✓" on every handled message forever (Chat.css `.chatbox-sent`). That is the standing mark the owner asked to remove; keep the tick only until handled, or hide it once ✓✓.

Stale doc: `ux/Dictate/doc/notes.md:762` still says both views draw "fast ✓ 0.4 s · smart ✓ 3.1 s" under the Prompt; V2 now draws the single moving `chat-v2-cursor` plus `chat-v2-smart-stamp`, and V1 draws ✓/✓✓. `ext/Chat/v2/readme.md` (line 13 and the class list) does not mention the cursor, smart stamp or smart-dots; `ext/Chat/readme.md` does not mention the three `send_on_*` settings (only `doc/mic-notes.md` does).

Untracked debug file `ext/Chat/v2/fixture/dbg-27008.jsonl` sits in the fixture folder; either index it in `v2/fixture/files.jsonl` with a purpose or move it out.

Mic.js `had_speech_q` is pushed in `close_segment` and shifted in `commit`; if a close_segment throws or a commit comes without a matching close (the Send path), the queue shifts out of step. The `?? this.has_speech` fallback only covers an empty queue. No test covers the hallucination drop or `cut_re()`.

`cut_re()` honours `send_on_period/question/comma` but `ends_sentence()` (Mic.js, just below) still tests the full `.!?…` set, so unchecking a mark changes where sends cut but not what counts as a finished sentence.
